 Amrita Rao reveals why she kept her son gadget-free for five years, sharing insights on screen-free parenting, motherhood, her relationship with RJ Anmol and career choices. 
 MC Lifestyle Desk 
 November 02, 2026 / 19:56 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 No TV, No Gadgets For 5 Years! Amrita Rao Reveals Her Parenting Choice For Son 
 In an age when smartphones, tablets and television screens have become an integral part of children's lives, actor Amrita Rao and her husband, RJ Anmol, took a different approach to parenting. The couple chose to raise their son without television or gadgets for the first five years of his life, a decision the actress recently opened up about during a candid conversation on the ThinkRight podcast.
 Known for her performances in films such as Vivah, Ishq Vishk and Main Hoon Na, Amrita spoke to Rajan Navani and spiritual leader BK Shivani about motherhood, relationships, personal choices and the importance of staying true to oneself.
 Recalling her approach to raising her son, Amrita said, “The best part of motherhood was that I kept my baby gadget-free for at least 5 years of his life.” The family also chose not to have a television at home during this period, making screen-free living a conscious parenting decision.
 The actress also reflected on the realities of becoming a parent and how global uncertainties can influence decisions about having children.
 Speaking about the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact on her perspective, Amrita said, “If COVID had happened before my pregnancy, I would have never brought a soul into this world.”
 Clarifying her thoughts, she explained that the statement was not an expression of regret about motherhood. Instead, she highlighted the importance of understanding the emotional, practical and long-term responsibilities that come with raising a child.
 According to Amrita, couples should have honest conversations about parenthood before deciding to bring a child into the world, rather than approaching it as an automatic next step in a relationship.
 Amrita also spoke about her relationship with radio personality RJ Anmol and why the couple chose to keep their romance away from the public eye for several years.
 Reflecting on the excitement of being in a new relationship and the temptation to announce it to everyone, she said, “Aapko chhat pe khada hoke, poore gaon ko batana hai ki I am dating somebody.”
 However, she believes that allowing a relationship to develop privately can help couples understand each other better, without external opinions or public scrutiny.
 “But initially, it’s for your betterment only and the betterment of the relationship that you explore each other without anyone knowing about it,” she added.
 The actress's reflections underline the importance of giving relationships time and space to grow, rather than allowing outside expectations to influence personal decisions.
 The conversation also touched upon the expectations placed on women after becoming mothers, particularly the pressure to put their professional ambitions on hold.
 Amrita believes that continuing to work is not necessarily just about earning money or achieving financial independence. For many women, professional engagement can also provide mental stimulation, a sense of identity and personal fulfilment.
 Sharing her perspective, she said, “Do not lose yourself in the zeal or attempt of becoming another person’s idea of success.”
 She further emphasised, “You have to be true to your definition of success.”
 Her message is particularly relevant for women navigating the demands of motherhood alongside their professional aspirations. According to the actress, success should be a personal choice rather than something dictated by societal expectations or conventional milestones.
 Amrita also reflected on her career and the enduring popularity of Vivah, which completes 20 years in November 2026.
 Recalling how the film was initially perceived as old-fashioned at a time when Hindi cinema was embracing changing storytelling trends, the actress said that it eventually found a special place in the hearts of audiences.
 Describing the film's connection with viewers, she said, “Ye ghar ghar ka ek film tha, iss film ne, iss kirdar ne sabke dilon mein ghar kar liya.”
 Amrita also spoke about staying committed to roles that aligned with her personal comfort and values, even as expectations within the film industry continued to evolve.
 From choosing a screen-free environment for her son to keeping her relationship private and defining professional success on her own terms, Amrita Rao's conversation offers a glimpse into the personal choices that have shaped her life. Her reflections also highlight a larger conversation around conscious parenting, individual identity and the freedom to make decisions that work for one's family.
